findings.suggested_fix: Update draft lines 98, 548, and 551, along with Table 1 (figures/avg_performance_allstates.tex), to report validation gains under a consistent fixed middle initial (16.0% under Ancestry or 11.5% under FamilySearch for the target group; 0.1% or 0.6% overall), and state explicitly that the validator is held constant across link versions.
findings.title: The paper's headline 28 percent match-quality gain is contradicted by the new fixed-validator diagnostic
findings.what_the_code_does: The paper reports that match quality (share of links validated by matching middle initials) increased from 65% to 84%, a 28 percent improvement in the target group (lines 98, 548) and by 1 percent overall (line 551). The upstream analysis in CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:73,83 produced this by evaluating links before using Ancestry's 1940 middle initial and after using a different 1940 middle initial from the new link file. The new diagnostic in replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:63-80 rescores both link versions against a single fixed 1940 middle initial from Ancestry or FamilySearch. Under Ancestry's fixed initial, target-group validation rises from 64.3% to 74.5% (a 16.0% gain, raw=15.96%), and all-records validation is essentially flat at 84.86% to 84.91% (a 0.1% gain, raw=0.067%). Under FamilySearch's fixed initial, target validation rises from 72.9% to 81.3% (an 11.5% gain, raw=11.51%), and all-records validation rises by 0.6%.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper claims a 28 percent increase in match quality as one of its three headline findings in the abstract and results section. The committed results in validation_fixed_initials.tex prove that nearly half of the target-group gain (and essentially all of the 1% overall gain) was driven by changing the measuring instrument between files rather than true link quality improvement.

findings.how_to_check: Run python replication/check_claims.py --paper-repo D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb. It reports MATCH for results-validated and intro-val-gain using create_figures_SSHA2025.tex while none of the validation_fixed_initials.tex macros are evaluated.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire results-validated and intro-val-gain in replication/claims.toml to the macros generated by validation_fixed_initials.tex (or update create_figures_SSHA2025.do to use the fixed initial), so that the checker alerts the authors until the text is aligned with the fixed-initial results.
findings.title: The automated claims checker gives false assurance because validation claims remain wired to the stale, disproven result file
findings.what_the_code_does: In replication/claims.toml:355-361, claim results-validated ('increased from 65\\% to 84\\%, a 28 percent improvement') and intro-val-gain ('28 percent increase in match quality') are mapped exclusively to valGainTarget and shareValTargetBefore/After from create_figures_SSHA2025.tex. Although validation_fixed_initials.tex is read by check_claims.py (claims_report.md:10), none of its macros (valGainAncTarget, valGainFsTarget) are checked in claims.toml. Consequently, check_claims.py reports 50 MATCH / 0 FAIL, certifying the draft claims against the superseded file while ignoring the diagnostic that disproved them.
findings.why_it_matters: The replication test suite serves to catch discrepancies between the text and empirical calculations. Leaving validation claims wired to the old file provides false confidence that the paper's headline 28% match quality claim is replicated and valid.

findings.how_to_check: Examine replication/results/validation_fixed_initials.tex. It contains only rate macros (val*) and agreement shares (agree*), completely lacking any n*, nMi*, or pctMi* macros or Kept/Switched categories.
findings.suggested_fix: In replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do, add Kept and Switched to the loop at line 81, and export n, nMi, and pctMi using repnum for all status categories and samples, matching validation_by_link_status.do.
findings.title: validation_fixed_initials.do omits Kept and Switched link validation and fails to export sample counts and initial availability
findings.what_the_code_does: In replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:81-88, the loop only summarizes and exports Added and Dropped links, omitting Kept (status 1) and Switched (status 2). Additionally, although non-missing counts are computed in locals nb, na, and nn (lines 73, 76, 85), none of the link sample sizes, counts with non-missing initials, or initial coverage percentages (pctMi) are exported to validation_fixed_initials.tex, unlike in validation_by_link_status.do:71-74.
findings.why_it_matters: Kept links constitute the large majority of linked records. Without exporting Kept validation under fixed initials, readers cannot see the invariant anchor uniting the before and after rates. Omitting the counts also conceals that fixed-initial validation is evaluated on only ~20-25% of linked records with observed initials.

findings.how_to_check: Run count if inlist(lower(word(strtrim(namefrst), 2)), "jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv") in temp.dta to verify the number of records where a generational suffix is parsed as a middle initial.
findings.suggested_fix: In replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:26, add a condition to set mi_\`src' = "" if inlist(lower(word(strtrim(\`v'), 2)), "jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv").
findings.title: Middle-initial parsing treats generational suffixes like 'Jr' and 'II' as middle initials without filtering
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 25 extracts the first character of the second word in the first-name field: gen mi_\`src' = lower(substr(word(strtrim(\`v'), 2), 1, 1)), and line 26 requires only that it be a letter [a-z]. For names containing generational suffixes in the second position (e.g. 'John Jr', 'William II'), this extracts 'j' or 'i' as the middle initial.
findings.why_it_matters: Individuals with generational suffixes are assigned bogus middle initials, contaminating middle-initial validation comparisons between 1930 and 1940 records.

findings.what_the_code_does: run_machineA.do:80-93 and Run-MachineA.ps1 execute only scripts in CODE/. Neither validation_fixed_initials.do, validation_by_link_status.do, nor middle_initial_sources.do is invoked by the replication driver.
findings.why_it_matters: A replicator running the standard replication harness will not regenerate validation_fixed_initials.tex. As intermediate data files evolve, the diagnostic outputs will silently become stale.

structured_output.summary: Commit range 5620c2b..HEAD introduces diagnostic scripts demonstrating that the paper's headline 28 percent match-quality gain (and 1 percent overall gain) was largely an artifact of shifting the 1940 middle-initial transcription between link files rather than true link recovery. When evaluated against a single fixed middle initial, the target-group validation gain falls to 16.0% (Ancestry) or 11.5% (FamilySearch), while overall validation is essentially flat (+0.1% or +0.6%). The single most important fix is to update the manuscript text and Table 1 to report match quality under a consistent fixed validator, and to wire the automated claims checker to these fixed-validator outputs.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
